x_failures: Blockquote attributed to Herold p.809, "The Ouroboros... represents the world and the cyclical nature of time. Its scales are said to represent the stars...", is not on the page; it is an invented paraphrase of Horapollo's text, and the page never says 'cyclical nature of time'.
reason: X's Pandora and Bosch citations hold up, but its Herold blockquote is an invented quotation and not the page's actual wording. Y's cited claims (Pandora p.270 dragon swallowing its tail, Böhme's fire-wheel of the essence in snake form, Khunrath's Saturn as Time and 'Tempus edax rerum') are broadly supported, though its reading of Böhme's passage is somewhat stretched.
